Thought: I need to determine which of the given gases are denser than air. To do this, I'll need to compare the molecular weights of each gas to that of air.

Air is primarily a mixture of nitrogen (78%) and oxygen (21%), with small amounts of other gases. The average molecular weight of air is approximately 29 g/mol.

Let me analyze each option:
A. Acetylene (C₂H₂) - Molecular weight is about 26 g/mol
B. Hydrogen (H₂) - Molecular weight is 2 g/mol
C. Natural gas (primarily methane, CH₄) - Molecular weight is about 16 g/mol
D. Propane (C₃H₈) - Molecular weight is about 44 g/mol

Comparing with air (29 g/mol):
- Acetylene (26 g/mol) is less dense than air
- Hydrogen (2 g/mol) is much less dense than air
- Natural gas/methane (16 g/mol) is less dense than air
- Propane (44 g/mol) is more dense than air

So among the given options, only propane is denser than air.
